title: IS-GPS-200N: Navstar GPS Space Segment/Navigation User Segment Interfaces
summary: The interface specification defining GPS L1/L2 signals, PRN codes and the legacy and CNAV navigation messages that every GPS receiver implements.
key_takeaways: Authoritative source for ephemeris and clock equations
Defines L1 C/A and L2C signal structure
Needed to build or audit any navigation message decoder

title: Interface Control Documents
summary: Index of current GPS interface specifications, including IS-GPS-200 (L1/L2), IS-GPS-705 (L5) and IS-GPS-800 (L1C).
key_takeaways: Single entry point for all GPS signal ICDs
Historic versions also linked
Archive site, frozen since February 2025 per its own banner

title: Galileo Open Service Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document (OS SIS ICD), Issue 2.1
summary: Defines Galileo E1, E5a, E5b open service signals, spreading codes and the F/NAV and I/NAV navigation messages.
key_takeaways: Required for decoding Galileo navigation data
I/NAV is the carrier for OSNMA bits

title: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication (OSNMA) Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document (SIS ICD), Issue 1.1
summary: Specifies Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication: the TESLA-based key chain, MAC and key messages carried in I/NAV, and the public key/Merkle tree structure.
key_takeaways: Civil signal authentication is available today on Galileo E1-B
Receivers need loose time synchronization to verify TESLA keys
Defines what an authenticated vs unauthenticated navigation message means

title: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication (OSNMA) Receiver Guidelines, Issue 1.3
summary: Implementation guidance for OSNMA receivers covering time synchronization requirements, cryptographic material handling, and how to use authentication results in the position solution.
key_takeaways: Explains which attacks OSNMA does and does not stop (e.g. replay/meaconing limits)
Covers key renewal and alert handling

title: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication (OSNMA)
summary: Official entry point for OSNMA status, public keys, Merkle tree root and related documentation.
key_takeaways: Where to download the cryptographic material receivers need

title: Programme Reference Documents
summary: Library of Galileo ICDs, service definition documents and performance reports for OS, HAS, OSNMA and SAR.
key_takeaways: Includes the HAS (High Accuracy Service) ICD for free PPP corrections

title: Navipedia
summary: ESA's wiki on GNSS fundamentals, systems, signals, algorithms and applications, including integrity (RAIM), PPP and interference topics.
key_takeaways: Best free reference for GNSS concepts
Good RAIM and error-model explanations

title: EUSPA GNSS Market and User Technology Reports
summary: Download page for EUSPA's market reports and GNSS User Technology Reports, which survey receiver, antenna and resilience technology trends.
key_takeaways: User Technology Report covers anti-jamming, authentication and multi-constellation trends
Useful for framing a pitch

title: GPSJam: daily maps of GPS interference
summary: Daily world maps of likely GPS interference derived from aircraft ADS-B navigation accuracy reports (NIC/NACp) aggregated from airplanes.live and ADS-B Exchange.
key_takeaways: Shows persistent interference zones (Baltic, Middle East, Black Sea)
Method is indirect: inferred from aircraft-reported accuracy

title: Flightradar24 GPS jamming map
summary: Flightradar24's map of GNSS interference, computed from navigation integrity category values broadcast by aircraft over its receiver network.
key_takeaways: Grey areas mean insufficient flights or receivers, not absence of jamming
Covers all GNSS, not just GPS

title: Assessing the Spoofing Threat: Development of a Portable GPS Civilian Spoofer
summary: Landmark ION GNSS 2008 paper that built a receiver-based civil GPS spoofer and analysed how hard it is to detect, kicking off modern civil spoofing defense research.
key_takeaways: Receiver-based spoofers can align with authentic signals and drag the victim smoothly
Simple checks are insufficient against a sophisticated spoofer
Motivates cryptographic and signal-level defenses

title: GNSS Spoofing and Detection
summary: Proceedings of the IEEE survey of spoofing attack types and detection/mitigation techniques, from navigation-data checks to signal distortion monitoring and multi-antenna methods.
key_takeaways: Taxonomy of defenses: cryptographic, signal-processing, geometric
Multi-antenna angle-of-arrival checks are powerful
Combining several weak tests beats any single test

title: Texas Spoofing Test Battery (TEXBAT)
summary: Public set of recorded high-rate IQ files of GPS L1 spoofing scenarios (static and dynamic, time and position push) used as a standard benchmark for spoofing detection.
key_takeaways: De facto benchmark for signal-level spoofing detectors
Recordings are large IQ files suitable for GNSS-SDR
Terms: research use only, (c) University of Texas; users asked not to redistribute the data

title: Signal Structure of the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
summary: Reverse-engineers the Starlink Ku-band downlink as OFDM and identifies synchronization sequences usable for opportunistic ranging and positioning.
key_takeaways: Starlink frames contain known sequences usable as pilots
Enables LEO signals-of-opportunity PNT without operator cooperation

title: The First Carrier Phase Tracking and Positioning Results With Starlink LEO Satellite Signals
summary: IEEE TAES letter showing carrier-phase tracking of Starlink signals with unknown structure and positioning from several satellites.
key_takeaways: Positioning from Starlink is feasible without knowing the signal format
Six satellites tracked; 7.7 m horizontal error with known receiver altitude

title: Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2023-2024
summary: Kaggle competition with Android raw GNSS and IMU logs plus ground truth, aiming at decimeter-level smartphone positioning.
key_takeaways: Large public smartphone GNSS dataset with truth
Winning solutions used factor graphs and carrier phase
Data also on IEEE DataPort under CC BY; Kaggle competition rules not verified

title: Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2022
summary: Earlier edition of the smartphone decimeter challenge with raw GNSS logs from multiple phones on US highways.
key_takeaways: Good secondary dataset for testing detectors on diverse phones

title: Android Raw GNSS Measurement Datasets for Precise Positioning
summary: ION GNSS+ 2020 paper releasing the first public Android raw GNSS datasets with corrections and ground truth, the origin of the GSDC series.
key_takeaways: Describes data collection and ground truth
Basis for all later GSDC editions

title: Raw GNSS Measurements
summary: Android documentation on the GnssMeasurement API: which phones expose pseudorange, carrier phase and AGC, and how to log them.
key_takeaways: AGC and C/N0 fields support jamming detection on phones
Duty cycling must be disabled for continuous carrier phase

title: NTRIP: Networked Transport of RTCM via Internet Protocol (BKG)
summary: BKG's overview of the NTRIP protocol for streaming GNSS corrections, with links to its caster, client and server software.
key_takeaways: NTRIP is HTTP-based streaming of RTCM
BKG maintains the reference caster

title: BKG Ntrip Client - BNC
summary: Page for BNC, BKG's multi-stream NTRIP client that records, decodes, converts to RINEX, monitors and can compute real-time PPP from correction streams.
key_takeaways: Swiss-army tool for real-time correction streams
Can monitor stream latency and outages

title: GNSS-SDR documentation
summary: Tutorials and reference for configuring the GNSS-SDR receiver, including signal processing blocks, front-end setup and monitoring outputs.
key_takeaways: Step-by-step first-fix tutorials with sample files
Explains each receiver block for modification

title: rtklibexplorer blog
summary: Long-running practical blog on low-cost RTK/PPK with RTKLIB demo5, u-blox receivers and smartphone data.
key_takeaways: Configuration recipes that save hours
Honest comparisons of receivers and settings

title: IGS products
summary: Catalog of International GNSS Service precise orbits, clocks, biases and atmospheric products used by PPP and precise processing.
key_takeaways: Precise products are free
Product latency ranges from real-time to final

title: A Software-Defined GPS and Galileo Receiver: A Single-Frequency Approach
summary: Textbook walking through a complete software GPS L1 receiver in MATLAB, from acquisition to position, the origin of SoftGNSS.
key_takeaways: Teaches acquisition and tracking loops by code
Still the standard SDR GNSS teaching text
